turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. What separates the high‑Tc tail from the rest?**
Sorting the 300 samples, essentially everything above ~90 K is a **layered cuprate** containing simultaneously **Cu + O + alkaline earth (Ba/Sr/Ca)**:

| composition | Tc (K) |
|---|---|
| H2S1 | 185 (outlier, high‑pressure hydride – not reachable with these variables) |
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132 |
| **Ba2Ca2Cu3O(≈8)** | **126** |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O | 120 |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Sr2Ca2Cu3Li0.2O | 117 |
| Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 | 110 |
| Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 109 |
| Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 106 |
| Ca0.285Sr0.665Cu1O2 | 100 |

**2. Element‑wise trends (mean Tc when present at non‑trivial fraction):**
- **Cu** present → mean Tc ≈ 70 K; absent → ≈ 12 K. Optimum Cu fraction is ~0.18–0.22 (Cu:O ≈ 1:2.7), i.e. the 3‑CuO₂‑layer stoichiometry. Pushing Cu to its max (0.45) corresponds to Cu‑rich/oxygen‑poor phases (e.g. CuO‑type, Cu₄.₅V₀.₅…) that do *not* do better.
- **O** in 0.50–0.60 is the sweet spot (Y‑123 ≈ 0.54, Bi‑2223 ≈ 0.53, Hg‑1223 ≈ 0.57). Larger O (→0.70) means insulating oxide‑rich phases.
- **Ca + Ba (+ a little Sr)** give the multilayer/charge‑reservoir blocks: Ba≈0.13, Ca≈0.11–0.14 reproduces the 120–132 K family. Sr‑only variants (Bi‑2223, 106–110 K) are slightly lower than Ba‑containing ones (126–132 K), so favor Ba with a trace of Sr.
- **Bi and Pb**: small amounts (Bi ~0.02–0.07, Pb ~0.01–0.03) appear in the 109–120 K Bi/Pb‑2223 family; but *large* Bi/Pb fractions (Bi‑2201 type, BaPbBiO₃ at 2.9 K, Pb metal) are bad. So keep them small, as dopants substituting the unavailable Hg/Tl site.
- **Detrimental / low‑Tc drivers:** Fe, As, Ni, V, Zn, Mo, Nb, B, C, Ce, Pr, Y, La. Every Fe‑As, B‑Mg/Mo/Zr, Nb, V, Ni, Zn‑metal and C‑rich entry sits below ~50 K; Ce/Pr suppress cuprate Tc (Pr‑doped YBCO drops, Ce‑doped 214 phases ≈ 16–20 K); La‑rich cuprates (La₂₋ₓSrₓCuO₄) top out near 35–45 K. Best to set all of these to 0 (Zn at 0.01–0.05 in YBCO only *lowers* Tc from 90 → 60–88 K).

**3. Target design**
Reproduce the Hg/Tl‑1223‑type "Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈" stoichiometry (the 126 K record within the allowed element set), with trace Bi/Pb/Sr occupying the charge‑reservoir site since Hg and Tl are unavailable:

O ≈ 0.53, Cu ≈ 0.20, Ba ≈ 0.13, Ca ≈ 0.11, Sr ≈ 0.01, Bi ≈ 0.01, Pb ≈ 0.01 (sums to 1.000; all within bounds).

This is Cu:Ba:Ca:O ≈ 3 : 2 : 1.7 : 8 with light Bi/Pb doping — the optimal hole‑doped triple‑CuO₂‑layer cuprate, expected Tc ≈ 125–135 K.

**Final: O=0.53, Cu=0.20, Ba=0.13, Sr=0.01, Y=0, Ca=0.11, La=0, Bi=0.01, Fe=0, Nb=0, C=0, Pr=0, As=0, B=0, Pb=0.01, Ce=0, Mo=0, V=0, Zn=0, Ni=0**
